paragraphs: On Sunday afternoon, Lily and Mia sat in Mia's kitchen. Mia opened the fridge and took out a bottle of cold juice. She filled two glasses. A small magnet in the shape of an octopus was on the door. "I got it at the aquarium," said Mia. "Now tell me about Green Hill." Lily came home from Grandma's house that morning.

"Green Hill is very different from our town," said Lily. "It is much quieter, because there is not much traffic." "Our town is noisier than the village," said Mia. "Yes, and it is busier, too," said Lily. "There are many shops in the town, but there is only one small shop in the village." "Is the air cleaner there?" asked Mia. "Yes, the air is fresh, and you can see more stars at night."

"What did you do there?" asked Mia. "I felt like an explorer," said Lily. "I discovered a path behind Grandma's house." "It goes through the trees to a small stream." "I want to go there!" said Mia. "A path in the village is not as short as a street in the town," said Lily. "But it is more fun." "If you come with me next time, we will walk there together."

"Did you do anything else?" asked Mia. "Grandpa and I made a kite," said Lily. "We flew it in the field behind the house, and it was a big success." "In the town, we cannot fly a kite in the street," said Mia. "The park is too small, and there are too many people." "That is true," said Lily. "But the town has the library and the aquarium." "The village has nothing like that."

"What do you want to become when you grow up?" asked Lily. "I want to become a vet," said Mia. "Do you want to work in the town or in the village?" "I will work in the town," said Mia, "but I will visit the village every month." She touched the octopus magnet on the fridge. "An octopus has eight arms," she said. "One arm is for the town, and one arm is for the village." Lily laughed and drank her juice.
